absent: Admin command execution internals, queueing, timeout and error mapping, and scatter list handling beyond command setup and drain marking.
List and capability initialization during admin activation and device parts enablement internals.
Shared queue finder, queue activation, vector synchronization, and notification payload encoding.
Ring transport feature acceptance and full version negotiation beyond the version one requirement.
PCI BAR mapping setup, common length and device length discovery, and MSI X vector allocation.
Identifier pool initialization and maximum object count discovery for device parts.
Hardened notification semantics beyond the broken flag update.
Configuration generation change protocol and concurrency rules for concurrent configuration access.

findings.text: Routine programs negotiated guest features into modern common configuration by stepping through selector values and writing low then high halves of each 64 bit word through selector and value registers.

Helpers expose device generation, device status, per queue reset and enable state, and configuration vector assignment over the modern common area. Status update is a single byte store without extra barrier. Generation and status reads return single bytes. Queue operations first select an index then touch reset or enable fields. Vector assignment writes the request then reads back the assigned value to confirm resources and flush the store.
Pair marks or clears a broken indicator on a virtual queue with ordered single writes that pair with a single read elsewhere for broken state observation.

Public routines query support for device parts handling and perform mode selection plus resource object lifecycle and metadata retrieval for virtual functions. Each operation resolves the physical function device from the passed PCI device, derives a virtual function identity, validates requested object and operation kinds, builds a small command descriptor with opcode and group selectors, executes it through the modern admin path, and maps allocation or execution failures to negative error codes. Creation allocates a bounded identifier from a pool and releases it on failure; successful destruction releases it.

Finalization first offers transport layers a chance to accept features, then requires the version one feature for modern operation and requires that common configuration length covers fields needed by enabled notification data, ring reset and admin queue features. Failure on either requirement aborts with an invalid argument result before features are programmed.

Transport acceptance enables SRIOV only when both the offered set includes it and the PCI device exposes the matching extended capability; ring reset and admin queue bits are accepted directly from the offered set.

Capability discovery queries a self scoped identifier list through the admin queue, assumes the supported set fits in one 64 bit word enforced at build time, converts the first word from device order, and proceeds to device parts enablement only when the device parts capability bit is present.

Device configuration accessors support only one, two, four and eight byte transfers with byte order conversion and split eight byte transfers into two four byte MMIO operations. Any other length is treated as a programming error, and accesses extending beyond the recorded device region length are rejected as programming errors.

Shared memory lookup walks vendor specific PCI capabilities, accepts only entries whose type indicates shared memory and whose identifier matches the request, rejects entries with unexpected length or with a BAR index outside the standard range, rebuilds 64 bit offset and length from low and high halves, verifies that offset plus length does not wrap and fits within the BAR length, then reports physical address plus offset and length.

Object creation accepts only the device parts object kind and get or set operation kinds and requires a nonzero maximum object count; destruction accepts only the device parts kind; metadata retrieval accepts only the size kind; parts retrieval accepts only the all kind. All paths require a resolvable physical function device and a valid virtual function identity, and use a member identity one greater than the virtual function number.

Removal and reinsertion of per queue bookkeeping into the shared virtual queue list are serialized by an interrupt saving spin lock held only around list mutation, with the node reinitialized when the queue has no callback or after removal.

Reset flushes pending callbacks after admin cleanup; per queue disable waits for an exclusive vector completion through interrupt synchronization without disabling the line to stay compatible with affinity managed interrupts.

Status is never set to zero through the normal setter; reset writes zero through the low level setter then polls the status byte with millisecond sleeps until it reads zero, which also flushes posted writes and device originated interrupts, then performs admin queue cleanup and flushes pending vector callbacks. Setting status with the driver ok bit additionally activates the admin queue.

Queue disable requires the ring reset feature, asserts reset through the modern common area, detaches the queue from interrupt handling, optionally marks the queue broken under a hardening option, waits for an exclusive vector if present, and marks a software reset flag. Re-enable is allowed only when that flag is set and both hardware reset and enable indicators read clear; it then reactivates the queue with its saved vector, rejoins interrupt handling when a callback exists, clears the broken mark when hardening applies, enables the queue in hardware, and clears the software flag.

Admin queue handling is inert unless the admin queue feature is negotiated. Activation initializes command list state and capability state. Cleanup returns early when the feature is absent or no queue is attached; otherwise it detaches every unused buffer, marks each command failed with an input output error, and signals its completion.

Configuration read and write entry points provide sized access to the device region; generation and status entry points delegate to modern MMIO helpers to return configuration generation and device status or to update status with activation side effects.

Queue discovery delegates to a shared finder and then enables every discovered queue in hardware as an irreversible step that can only be undone by reset. The data carrying notification path derives a 32 bit payload from the queue and writes it to the queue private notification address, always reporting success. Configuration vector selection delegates to the modern helper.

Out of range configuration accesses, zero status through the normal setter, and unsupported transfer widths trigger immediate bug handling. Device reset and queue reset or enable polling loop with millisecond sleeps until hardware clears the corresponding byte or word, which can delay the caller if the device never converges. Re-enabling a queue that was not in reset or whose hardware indicators remain set is rejected as busy, and disabling without the ring reset feature reports missing support.

Behaviour is keyed by feature selectors for version one, notification data, ring reset, admin queue and SRIOV; by admin opcodes for capability list query, device mode set, resource object create and destroy, device parts metadata get and parts get; by group selectors for self and SRIOV; by a device parts capability bit and command bitmap; and by shared memory capability typing with vendor capability walking and BAR plus offset plus length layout including high halves.

Modern common area exposes selector and value pairs for features, plus generation, status, queue select, reset and enable, admin queue count, notification data and MSI X configuration fields; the device area is a byte window with recorded length. Admin commands carry opcode, group type, member identity, optional data and result scatter entries, result length, return code and completion. Per queue state includes index, reset flag, callback, private notification address and saved vector; SHM results carry address and length.
Single byte MMIO helpers map directly to underlying byte read and write operations on volatile configuration addresses.
